name: tstmd-contraction-reorientation
title: Cell–ECM mechanical coupling (real TST-MD, 2D) — NOT reproduced
question: Does the real 2D static-adhesion hybrid CPM + bead-spring ECM engine (Tsingos et al. 2023, the published ancestor of Merks' 3D model) reproduce the paper's core mechanical-reciprocity result — a contractile cell that drags its focal adhesions and the attached, crosslinked ECM inward, reorienting and densifying the matrix?
hypothesis: A contractile cell coupled to the fiber network via adhesions will pull those adhesions (and the crosslinked fibers they grip) toward its centre as it contracts, so the adhesion-ring radius and near-fiber density track the cell — reproducing Keijzer & Merks 2026 Fig 4.
objective: Run seeded coupled simulations through the real engine and measure, over the contraction, the cell area, the adhesion-ring radius, the near-fiber radius, and fiber reorientation q/q0 — testing whether the ECM is dragged inward.
description: REAL output of the TST-MD engine, driven CPU-only via the viva-tstmd Docker bridge (TST C++ + HOOMD + MUSCLE3). This study evaluates the paper-faithful coupling bar and FAILS it: across every parameter regime tried (fiber stiffness stiff->soft, crosslink density, contractility lambda up to 400, MD noise md_kT, adhesion-annihilation penalty, gradient vs uniform displacement selection) the cell contracts but its adhesions stay frozen in place — the cell detaches from the ECM rather than dragging it inward. This is the open cell-ECM coupling / calibration gap, reported as a failing reproduction, not hidden.

behavior_tests.name: Cell drags its adhesions (and the ECM) inward as it contracts
behavior_tests.description: PAPER BAR (Keijzer & Merks 2026, Fig 4): a contracting cell pulls its focal adhesions and the attached crosslinked fibers toward its centre. Measure: the adhesion-ring radius should shrink substantially as the cell area falls. MEASURED (real engine): adhesion-ring radius stays ~58 px while the cell contracts from ~13000 to ~0 lattice sites (change < 2%). The cell detaches from its adhesions — coupling does NOT engage.
behavior_tests.pass_if: adhesion-ring radius decreases by >= 30% as the cell contracts
behavior_tests.paper_reference: Keijzer & Merks 2026, Fig 4A-D (cell drags/remodels the ECM)

behavior_tests.name: Fibers reorient strongly toward the cell (matrix remodeling)
behavior_tests.description: PAPER BAR: strong fiber reorientation toward the cell (q/q0 well above 1) and local densification as the matrix is pulled in. MEASURED: q/q0 rises only to ~1.09 and the densification factor stays ~0 (no accumulation) — far below a reproduction of the paper's remodeling; consistent with the ECM not being dragged inward.

evidence.from_test: Cell drags its adhesions (and the ECM) inward as it contracts
evidence.observed: adhesion-ring radius ~58 px, roughly constant, while cell area 13000 -> ~0; bistable (hold at lambda<=3 vs collapse at lambda>=4)

findings.statement: The real TST-MD engine does NOT reproduce the paper's cell-ECM coupling. Engine instrumentation (rebuilt bin/adhesions, logged AdhesionMover) shows the CPM DOES move adhesions (876 commits, ~1.27px/frame) and the CPM->MD sync works — so it is NOT a sync bug. The obstruction is BISTABILITY: the ECM resistance adh_dh is ~constant (fibers aren't dragged -> no densification -> no stiffening feedback), so the engine only ever fully holds the cell (lambda<=3, no contraction) or lets it collapse leaving the adhesions behind (lambda>=4), even at 2000 MCS with gradient selection. No drag-to-new-equilibrium regime is reachable from any ymmsl parameter. See followup_proposals + viva-tstmd/docs/cell-ecm-coupling.md.

What DOES hold (sub-reproduction): the cell genuinely contracts (13000 -> ~0) and shows weak reorientation (q/q0 ~1.09). But these are not the paper's remodeling result; densification stays ~0. A real bridge bug (float-typed settings written as ints) was found + fixed while investigating, which unblocked the parameter search.

conclusion: FAILING reproduction. The real 2D engine contracts the cell but does not drag its adhesions / the crosslinked ECM inward — the mechanical coupling that produces Keijzer & Merks 2026's Fig-4 remodeling does not engage through any exposed parameter. Reproducing it needs the authors' exact configuration or deeper engine work (see investigation caveats).
key_assumptions: 2D (the engine is 2D; the target paper is 3D) — mechanism analog at best.
Static adhesions (as in the 3D paper), not the dynamic focal adhesions of Keijzer et al. 2025.
Reduced size vs the paper's HPC scale for CPU tractability.

followup_proposals.title: Refactor CellularPotts::DeltaH to floating point (stop int-rounding the ECM work)
followup_proposals.motivation: ca.cpp:575 does `DH += static_cast<int>(round(adh_dh))`, so sub-unit ECM resistance (soft fibers) is rounded to zero and never influences acceptance. Faithful mechanics need adh_dh to contribute continuously.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: Make DeltaH return/accumulate double across ca.cpp and the Metropolis step, then rebuild bin/adhesions (verified rebuildable in-container).

followup_proposals.title: Physical->internal unit-scaling from Frontiers Table 1 (escape bistability)
followup_proposals.motivation: The coupling is bistable — the ECM either fully holds the cell (lambda<=3) or the cell collapses leaving adhesions behind (lambda>=4); no drag-to-new-equilibrium regime is reachable from any ymmsl parameter, because adh_dh is ~constant (fibers aren't dragged -> no densification -> no stiffening feedback).
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: Derive internal spring_k/crosslink_k/lambda/target from Table 1 (K=Y*A/L, Y=1e6 Pa, fiber diam 0.125um) so adh_dh lands in the commensurate band AND grows with fiber stretch, igniting the drag->densify->stiffen feedback.

followup_proposals.title: Obtain the Merks lab's exact figure configuration
followup_proposals.motivation: Every public config is a demo build; the paper's contraction experiment parameters are not in the public code/docs. The definitive check.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: Retrieve the figure .par/.ymmsl from Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7906973 or by contacting the authors; diff against our regime.
